title: Plastic pollution
examples: Teacher, where does all that plastic actually end up?
What exactly are microplastics and are they dangerous?
What can we do to stop plastic from hurting animals?

explain.say: Today we will learn about plastic pollution in our world. We will see where this trash goes.
Sometimes plastic floats in the ocean for a very long time. It can get caught in currents. This makes big patches of trash.
Plastic can break down into tiny pieces called microplastics. These are very small to see. They are smaller than a grain of sand.
These tiny microplastics get into many things we need. They can even get into the food chain. This means they move up to us.

items: Source (e.g., tire wear): Microplastics enter environment

explain.say: We must find better solutions to reduce plastic waste. We can reuse items instead of throwing them away. This is called reducing waste.
In our everyday lives, we can choose reusable water bottles. This stops single-use plastic bottles from entering the environment.

faq.q: Are microplastics really dangerous to animals?
faq.a: Scientists are still studying the full effects, but they can cause harm by blocking digestive systems. It is best to reduce plastic use to help prevent this.
asks: What is the danger of tiny plastic bits?

faq.q: Does recycling everything really solve the problem?
faq.a: Recycling is very important, but it is not the only answer. We must also focus on reducing the amount of plastic we use in the first place.
asks: If we recycle a lot, is the planet safe?
Is recycling enough to stop pollution?

faq.q: Where does the plastic that is thrown in the street go?
faq.a: Much of it gets washed into storm drains and then into rivers. From there, it travels out to the ocean.
asks: Does litter go straight to the sea?
How does street trash reach the ocean?

faq.q: What is the difference between plastic pollution and littering?
faq.a: Littering is the act of dropping trash. Plastic pollution is the large-scale problem caused by that trash accumulating in the environment.
asks: Is littering the same as pollution?
What is the big picture problem with trash?

faq.q: Can plastic pollution affect us even if it is far from us?
faq.a: Yes, because the pollution travels through water and air currents. This means it can end up in the food sources we eat.
asks: Can I get sick from ocean plastic?
How far can plastic pollution travel?

facts: Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down completely in natural environments.
Microplastics can come from many sources, like clothing fibers and tires.
The 'Reduce' step in waste management means using less of something.
Large ocean currents help move plastic trash across vast distances.

quiz.say: Which action is the most effective way to stop plastic pollution at the source?
quiz.why: Reducing consumption stops the plastic from ever being made or used as waste.

wrong.0: Some plastic is necessary for safe medical equipment.
wrong.2: Recycling still requires energy and sometimes creates new waste.
wrong.3: This fixes the visible mess but does not stop the source of the pollution.

quiz.say: If plastic breaks into tiny pieces, what are those pieces called?
quiz.why: Microplastics specifically describe very small pieces of plastic pollution.

wrong.0: Macroplastics are the large, visible pieces of trash.
wrong.1: Debris is a general word for scattered waste, not the scientific term.
wrong.2: Pollutants are any harmful substances, not just the size of the plastic.

quiz.say: Which of these items is an example of 'reusing' plastic items?

options.show: Melting plastic to make new beads
options.say: Melting plastic to make new beads

options.show: Throwing it in the recycling bin
options.say: Throwing it in the recycling bin

quiz.why: Reusing means finding a new purpose for an item without changing it much.

wrong.1: This process is closer to recycling, which changes the material.
wrong.2: This is the process of recycling, not reusing the item itself.
wrong.3: Burning destroys the material and releases pollution.
